title: Vav
hookLine: a hook, and the word "and": it joins things

cards: In Exodus, Moses is given building plans for the Tabernacle, the tent where God's presence would dwell among the people. The list is detailed: boards, sockets, curtains of blue and purple and scarlet.
And somewhere in it, a tiny, practical part. Something has to hold the curtain up. The pillars get hooks of gold.
Nobody comes to see the hooks. But without them a beautiful curtain is a heap of cloth on the floor. The Hebrew word for those hooks is the name of today's letter.

teach.b: Three things hang on this little hook. First, the word. In the Tabernacle instructions, the hooks on the pillars are vavim, the plural of vav.
The King James puts it plainly: "their hooks shall be of gold."
The letter looks the part: a single upright stroke with a small bend at the top, like a peg on a wall. Second, a job. In Hebrew, "and" isn't a separate word.
It's this letter, clipped onto the front of the next word: ve. Hooked on. Open Genesis in Hebrew and watch it work, sentence after sentence.

teach.h: AND GOD SAID… AND THERE WAS.
teach.b: The King James keeps many of the hooks: "And God said, Let there be light: and there was light." Each part of creation is fastened to the one before, and the story never lets go of the thread. Third, a surprise.
Sometimes vav stops being a consonant and carries a vowel, an o or an oo. In shalom, the o you hear in the middle is held up by a vav. The letter that joins sentences also joins sounds.
That's vav's whole character: rarely the point of the sentence, and the sentence falls apart without it. A lot of good work looks like that. The person who introduces two friends.
The text that says, I'll come with you. A small and that keeps two things from falling apart.

how: Children learning Hebrew may meet vav early, both as a letter and as the prefix ve-, 'and'; readers of the Hebrew Bible hear it at the start of verse after verse in the stories of Genesis.

games.q: you're translating Genesis 1 into English, and sentence after sentence starts with a vav. what does the King James do?
o: keeps them: "and God said… and there was light."
drops them, so the sentences stand alone.
games.why: the King James keeps the hooks: "And God said, Let there be light: and there was light." each part of creation hangs on the one before.

practice: Look around your life for two things sitting apart that belong together: two friends who'd like each other, a family member and a phone call, a good intention and its first small step.
Don't fix anything yet; just let the word and sit between them, this and that, and feel what it would take to hook them together. If you pray, bring both into your prayer at once.

wordCard.voice: Vav. A hook, like the gold hooks of the Tabernacle; the letter that means and, and sometimes carries a vowel. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: the letter vav, also the word for a hook (Exodus 26:32).

carryVoice: Your line: vav connects. The smallest and can hold a whole story together. See you tomorrow.
